historical_commentary.text: This note tackles form resizing logic beyond 4D's basic built-in resize/move behaviors, providing a combined language-based method for computing object placement and size during form resize events. The core problem — precisely controlling how form objects reposition and resize together — remains conceptually relevant, but the note's approach is grounded in Design Mode's binary form structure and language commands of that era; current 4D forms still support similar resizing logic (and later versions added more built-in responsive/auto-resize capabilities), making the specific technique here a useful historical reference rather than the state of the art.
related_updates: Later 4D versions introduced more built-in form object anchoring/auto-resize options, reducing the need for fully custom resize methods in many common cases
4D's form and object model has continued to evolve, though the general on-form resize event and language-based approach described remains structurally similar today
